deck.title: Cognito
deck.analogy: An office building: the User Pool is the login box that gives you a visitor badge (JWT), and the Identity Pool is the exchange desk that swaps it for a keycard (temporary AWS credentials).

cards.front: What two problems does Amazon Cognito solve for app customers?

back.answer: "Who are you?" (authentication, User Pools) and "what AWS resources may you touch?" (authorization, Identity Pools).
back.explanation: Cognito answers both with two deliberately different pieces.
back.mnemonic: Office building: login box (User Pool) + exchange desk (Identity Pool).

cards.front: In the Cognito analogy, what are the visitor badge and the keycard?

back.answer: The badge is the JWT from a User Pool; the keycard is the temporary AWS credentials from an Identity Pool.
back.explanation: The badge alone doesn't open doors; you swap it at the exchange desk for credentials.
back.mnemonic: Badge = JWT; keycard = temp AWS creds.

cards.front: What do JWT, STS and IdP stand for in Cognito context?

back.answer: JWT = JSON Web Token; STS = Security Token Service; IdP = Identity Provider.
back.explanation: JWT proves authentication; STS mints short-lived AWS credentials; an IdP vouches for identity (Google, Facebook, SAML).

cards.front: Cognito User Pools vs Identity Pools: what question does each answer?

back.answer: User Pools: authentication (who are you?). Identity Pools: authorization for AWS (what AWS resources may you touch?).
back.explanation: This is the core Cognito distinction.
back.mnemonic: User Pool = login box; Identity Pool = exchange desk.

cards.sourceHeading: The core distinction (THE thing to know)

cards.front: What is a Cognito User Pool versus a Cognito Identity Pool?

back.answer: User Pool is a user directory (sign-up, sign-in, password resets); Identity Pool is a credential exchange desk.

cards.sourceHeading: The core distinction (THE thing to know)

cards.front: What does each Cognito component return: User Pools vs Identity Pools?

back.answer: User Pools return JWT tokens; Identity Pools return temporary AWS credentials (via STS).

cards.sourceHeading: The core distinction (THE thing to know)

cards.front: Which Cognito component provides Hosted UI, MFA, social login and SAML IdPs, and which provides guest access?

back.answer: User Pools: Hosted UI, MFA, social login (Google/Facebook/Apple), SAML. Identity Pools: guest access and fine-grained per-user IAM permissions.

cards.sourceHeading: The core distinction (THE thing to know)

cards.front: What does each Cognito component plug into: User Pools vs Identity Pools?

back.answer: User Pools plug into API Gateway and ALB as an authorizer; Identity Pools give apps direct access to S3, DynamoDB, any AWS API.

cards.sourceHeading: The core distinction (THE thing to know)

cards.front: Trap: mobile app users must access S3 directly. Why is "Cognito User Pools" the wrong answer?

back.answer: A JWT can't call S3; only AWS credentials can. Direct AWS resource access means Identity Pools.
back.explanation: User Pools give tokens, not AWS credentials.
back.mnemonic: Badge doesn't open doors; keycard does.

cards.sourceHeading: The core distinction (THE thing to know)

cards.front: Describe the classic Cognito flow from login to calling S3.

back.answer: User logs in to User Pool → gets JWT → Identity Pool swaps it via STS → temp AWS credentials → app calls S3/DynamoDB directly.
back.explanation: User Pool is the login box; Identity Pool is the exchange desk.
back.mnemonic: Login box → badge → exchange desk → keycard.
back.code: User login -> User Pool -> JWT -> Identity Pool -> (STS) -> temp AWS creds -> S3/DynamoDB

cards.sourceHeading: The classic flow (draw this in your head)

cards.front: Which tokens can a Cognito Identity Pool accept for exchange?

back.answer: Tokens from a User Pool, social providers directly, or SAML — any recognized badge.
back.explanation: The Identity Pool doesn't require a User Pool.
back.mnemonic: Exchange desk for any recognized badge.

cards.sourceHeading: The classic flow (draw this in your head)

cards.front: What does a Cognito User Pool authorizer on API Gateway do?

back.answer: It validates the JWT before your backend runs, authenticating API users without writing auth code.
back.explanation: ALB can also authenticate through Cognito before forwarding requests.

cards.sourceHeading: The clever bits worth exam points

cards.front: How do Cognito Identity Pools let users browse before signing up?
cards.sourceHeading: The clever bits worth exam points

cards.front: How do you let each Cognito user access only their own S3 folder with one policy?

back.answer: Identity Pool + IAM policy variable ${cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:sub} scoping to s3://bucket/${id}/*.
back.explanation: One policy serves a million users with zero per-user setup.

cards.sourceHeading: The clever bits worth exam points

cards.front: Trap: employees need SSO to AWS accounts. Cognito or IAM Identity Center?

back.answer: IAM Identity Center (successor to AWS SSO), not Cognito.
back.explanation: Employees are workforce; Cognito is for customers of your app.
back.mnemonic: If they get a paycheck, Cognito is wrong.

cards.sourceHeading: Cognito vs IAM Identity Center — don't mix up the audiences

cards.front: Cognito vs IAM Identity Center: which audience does each serve?

back.answer: Cognito: customers of your app (millions of external users). IAM Identity Center: employees/workforce signing into AWS accounts and business apps.
back.mnemonic: Paycheck from the company → not Cognito.

cards.sourceHeading: Cognito vs IAM Identity Center — don't mix up the audiences

cards.front: A mobile app needs user sign-up, sign-in, and login with Google and Facebook. Which service?

choices.why: Issues AWS credentials, not a user directory.
User directory with social login and hosted UI.
Doesn't scale to millions of customers.

cards.front: Authenticated app users must upload files directly to S3 from the device. What do you use?

back.explanation: JWT → STS → temporary AWS credentials; only creds can call S3.

choices.why: Authenticates API calls, not direct S3 access.
Exchanges tokens for temporary AWS credentials.

cards.front: Users should browse limited content without creating an account. Which Cognito feature?

choices.why: Adds login security, not guest access.
A login page still requires an account.

cards.front: You must authenticate users of a REST API on API Gateway without custom code. What do you use?

back.explanation: API Gateway validates the JWT for you.

choices.why: The requirement is no custom code.
API Gateway validates the JWT natively.

cards.front: Each user may only read and write objects in their own S3 prefix. What is the solution?

choices.why: One policy scoped by the user's identity ID.

cards.front: Company employees need SSO access to multiple AWS accounts. Which service?

choices.why: Authenticates API calls, not account SSO.

cards.front: Enterprise customers must log into your SaaS app with their corporate SAML IdP. What do you use?

back.answer: Cognito User Pools with SAML federation.
back.explanation: Still authentication — still the login box.

choices.why: Provides AWS credentials, not the login directory.
For your workforce, not SaaS customers.

cards.front: You need to add MFA to your application's customer logins. Which Cognito piece?

choices.why: Mints credentials, doesn't handle MFA login.
